final_answer: Imagine a small town where every time the local ice cream truck arrives, a nearby pond experiences an increase in drowning incidents. At first glance, one might think eating ice cream causes people to drown. But wait—what if the real reason is that both events are linked to a third factor: hot weather? On hot days, more people buy ice cream to cool off, and more people also go swimming in the pond. The heat is the true cause of both the ice cream sales and the drownings. This shows that just because two things happen together (correlation), it doesn’t mean one causes the other (causation). Safe.
